meta.purpose: The process wiring: which modules exist, in what order, depending on what, under which pre/post gates. Per plan §2.2 the flow is DATA, not code — the orchestrator builds a run plan by reading this, and changing the pipeline is a config change.
meta.envelope: Every item carries the common rule envelope — see ../_manifest.json meta.envelope.
meta.authority: plan moonlit-launching-cocke §3.1C, §3.2, §3.3.4, §A.3; authored 2026-07-15 on the researcher's observation that the pipeline configuration was missing and that a pre-processing step before lexical was unaccounted for.

★ the_gap_the_researcher_found.the_observation: researcher 2026-07-15: 'to me your raw and fetch is in the same pipeline, but there is a pre-processing before lexical that I am missing. I dont see the pipeline configration yet.'
★ the_gap_the_researcher_found.verdict: CORRECT, and it is structural rather than a missing file. THE BASE LAYER HAS ALMOST NO PROCESS.

the_layer_analysis.base (layer 2): plan §3.4 says base = SPANS · PASSAGES · STEMS · SEEDS. Only PASSAGES has a process (`verses-passages`). SPANS: no process. STEMS: no process. SEEDS: live inside `characteristics`, which is an INTERPRETATION process holding a BASE artefact.
the_layer_analysis.interpretation (layer 3): lexical · characteristics · findings ✓ all three exist
the_layer_analysis.prose (layer 4): no process, and no module either — the nine end at findings.

★ the_gap_the_researcher_found.the_module_analysis: Of the plan's 9 modules, TWO map to no process: module 4 (Stem-master maintenance) and module 8 (Prepare data for analysis). The plan's own §A.11 lists 7 by-process rule-sets for 9 modules and never reconciles the difference. The gap was in the plan before it was in the config.

★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER.what_is_missing: SPAN CONSTRUCTION — deriving, from raw morphology, the addressable term-in-verse spans that everything above joins on. That is the pre-processing before lexical.
why_it_is_the_load-bearing_gap: plan §3.4.2 states it outright: 'the span-id IS the join key' — never Strong's-encoded endpoints
ent.lexical.record identity = span-id + ve_nr — every lexical read is ABOUT a span
ent.char.candidate identity = span-id — every candidate IS a span
ve_lexical.from_span / to_span — every pair's endpoints are spans
So the entire interpretation layer is addressed in a currency no process mints.
★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER.where_it_lives_today: Inside `audit_word`, which 'inserts + span-links terms and verses in one pass' (CLAUDE.md §8) — bundled with ingest, and reachable by a flag literally named `--skip-span-backpop`.
★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER.⚠ why_that_is_dangerous: A step everything joins on is SKIPPABLE, undocumented as a process, and has no gate of its own. `span_strong_match` is the field that proves a term is actually AT a verse — the difference between evidence and a reference — and it is produced by a bundled side-effect. A skipped backpop leaves spans absent; absent spans leave the lexical layer with nothing to read; and nothing announces it.
★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER.the_layer_violation: Span construction is DERIVATION from morphology, so by raw.definition it is BASE, not raw. Bundling it into the ingest module puts a base artefact inside a raw process — the same layer-mixing the plan forbids (§3.4.2 'no analytical values on mechanical tables'), one layer down.

★ the_gap_the_researcher_found.what_this_file_does_about_it: It states the modules and the wiring, and marks modules 4 and 8 (and the missing span module) explicitly rather than quietly omitting them. Whether to carve the base layer into processes is a researcher decision — see open.pipeline.base-layer-carve. This file does not pretend the gap is closed.

nodes.modules: The pipeline segments — one item per module, with order, handler, scope and the process it governs.
nodes.dependencies: The dependency graph — one item per edge, with activation (auto | halt).
nodes.module_gates: Which gates run pre/post per module, and what a failure does.

meta.the_flow: 1 STEP ingest -> 2 Seed maintenance -> {3 Prepare passage, 4 Stem master} -> 5 Prepare lexical -> 6 Characteristic maintenance -> 7 Data validation -> 8 Prepare for analysis -> 9 Findings. Arrows are DEPENDENCIES, not hard-coded calls (plan §3.2).

open.issue: The base layer (spans · passages · stems · seeds) has one process for passages, none for spans or stems, and its seeds sit inside an interpretation process. The `governs` vocabulary has no value for spans or stems, so a module for them cannot even declare what it governs.
open.consequence: The pre-processing between raw and lexical is unconfigured and therefore ungoverned — no rules, no gates, no home. It is also the step the whole interpretation layer's addressing depends on.
options: A: ONE `base` process — spans + stems + passages + seeds together. Simple; but it swallows `verses-passages`, which is already authored and has real genre-routing rules of its own, and it makes one process own four unrelated derivations.

B: THREE processes — add `spans` and `stems` alongside the existing `verses-passages`; seeds stay with `characteristics`. Keeps the existing carve, mirrors the module list (3 = passages, 4 = stems, + a new span module), and each has genuinely different rules.

C: spans fold into `raw` — treat span-linking as part of ingest, as audit_word does today. REJECTED: spans are DERIVED, so by raw.definition they are base, and raw.immutable would then govern a derived artefact that changes whenever its derivation rule changes.
open.recommendation: B. Spans and stems have nothing in common except being derived: a span is an ADDRESS (the join key for everything above), a stem is a LINGUISTIC DERIVATION. Bundling them under one `base` process would produce exactly the kind of catch-all that the failure record calls over-structuring. C is how it works today and is precisely what hides the step.
open.resolve_by: researcher decision — BLOCKS a complete pipeline; modules 4 and the span module cannot declare `governs` until it is ruled

open.issue: The candidate seed is BASE per plan §3.4.1 ('Base — derived: passages, stems, seed/candidate stamping | Regenerate'), but char.seed-layers and ent.char.candidate live in process/characteristics.json, an interpretation process.
open.consequence: An interpretation process owns a base artefact. Already flagged from the other side in characteristics.json (ent.char.candidate: 'layer: base (mechanical seed) — but the screen0 verdict is INTERPRETATION and must not live on this row').
open.recommendation: Split by layer, not by topic: the mechanical seed (which spans are candidates) is BASE; the Screen-0 verdict and the role (what a candidate IS) are INTERPRETATION. They are already two facts on one row, which is the actual defect — the live DB stamps role/char_candidate onto verse_span_index, and the migration strips exactly that (plan 3.4.1).

open.issue: Module 8 (Prepare data for analysis) governs no process. Prose (layer 4) has neither a process nor a module — the nine end at findings.
open.consequence: The study's END POINT is two-part: an evidenced findings corpus AND the products drawn from it (essays, study guides, books). The second part has no pipeline at all.
open.recommendation: Defer both, deliberately and on the record. The plan itself parks them ('Analysis & findings (least-defined): the study's higher-order outputs sit beyond segment 9'). Not a gap to close now — but it should be a KNOWN debt, not a silence, because it is half the stated end point.

open.issue: The researcher observed that raw and fetch are 'in the same pipeline'. They are: module 1 (Get data from STEP) performs both, and they are separate PROCESSES but not separate MODULES.
open.consequence: Not a defect — process and module are different axes and need not be 1:1. But it means module 1's post-gates must cover BOTH processes' controls, and a module that spans two processes loads two rule-sets.
open.recommendation: Keep them as one module and two processes, and let this be the worked example that process != module. Splitting them would gain nothing: a fetch that does not store is useless, and a raw write with no fetch cannot happen. The rules differ; the execution does not.
open.resolve_by: no decision needed — recorded so the asymmetry is deliberate

modules.subject: module-ingest
modules.intent: Retrieve from STEP and store the raw measure layer — verse, morphology, lexicon.
modules.satisfaction: The requested scope's raw layer is present, complete against the oracle, and provenance-stamped.

spec.note: Spans TWO processes (fetch = what to retrieve, raw = what is stored). See open.pipeline.raw-fetch-coupling — deliberate, not an oversight.
spec.⚠ currently_also_does: SPAN-LINKING (audit_word 'inserts + span-links in one pass'). That is base-layer work bundled into ingest — it belongs to the missing span module. See meta.★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER.

modules.subject: module-seed
modules.intent: Maintain the registry and the candidate seed — which spans are nominated for reading.
modules.satisfaction: The seed is built through all layers, over-inclusive, and every candidate resolves to a verse-record.

spec.⚠ layer_note: The seed is BASE (plan §3.4.1) but its rules live in the characteristics process. See open.pipeline.seed-layer-home.

modules.subject: module-passage
modules.intent: Build passages — maximal runs of consecutive candidate-bearing verses — and verse coverage.
modules.satisfaction: Every candidate-bearing verse belongs to a passage; coverage arithmetic reconciles.

modules.subject: module-stem
modules.reference: plan §3.3.4; plan §4 ('No dedicated stem-master table exists — derive from verse_morphology')
modules.intent: Build and maintain the stem master, derived from morphology.
modules.satisfaction: Every attested stem is in the master, derived from morph_code.

spec.⚠ governs_is_a_placeholder: `raw` is WRONG and is set only because the envelope requires a value and no correct one exists. A stem is DERIVED from morph_code, so it is BASE, not raw (raw.definition). This module cannot honestly declare what it governs until the base-layer carve is ruled.
spec.note: No stem-master table exists in the live DB (plan §4). This is a genuinely new build, not a rewrite.

modules.subject: module-lexical
modules.intent: The interpretive core — per passage/characteristic, produce the genre-mandatory ledger via the API adapter, gated by the validation engine.
modules.satisfaction: Every span in scope carries its ledger's dimensions, every value passes its gates.

spec.⚠ blocked: process/lexical.json carries 6 RECONCILE items; recon.mandatory-ledger is the hard one — without the ledger, 'complete' is undefined.
spec.⚠ its_input_has_no_producer: This module reads SPANS. No module builds them (meta.★ THE_SPAN_LAYER_IS_THE_ANSWER). Its dependency chain currently runs to module 1 by accident, because span-linking is bundled there.

modules.subject: module-characteristic
modules.intent: Derive and maintain ib_characteristic; write back roles. Families/clusters remain disposable scaffolding.
modules.satisfaction: Every read span has a role; characteristics are keyed on meaning-in-context.

spec.⚠ blocked: recon.role-enum blocks this module AND module 5.

modules.subject: module-validation
modules.intent: The full gate battery + scoreboard — AND every other module's pre/post gate.
modules.satisfaction: Every gate in scope has run; the scoreboard is current.

spec.dual_role: It is BOTH a standalone module AND the gate every other module calls. This is where 'done = verse-level validity, not coverage' is enforced.
spec.note: A utility, not a study process — which is why it governs util.validation.

modules.subject: module-analysis-prep
modules.intent: Projections and extracts for downstream analysis.
modules.satisfaction: Projections regenerable from the DB; nothing authoritative lives only in them.

spec.⚠ governs_is_a_placeholder: `findings` is a guess. This module has no process of its own — see open.pipeline.module-8-and-prose.

modules.subject: module-findings
modules.intent: Capture and produce evidenced findings from validated lexicals.
modules.satisfaction: Every finding is verse-grounded, STATED-vs-INFERRED marked, and traceable.

modules.subject: module-spans
modules.authority: researcher observation 2026-07-15 ('there is a pre-processing before lexical that I am missing'); derived from plan §3.4.2 ('the span-id is the join key')
modules.intent: ★ THE MISSING MODULE. Derive the addressable term-in-verse spans from raw morphology — the currency every layer above is addressed in.
modules.satisfaction: Every term-in-verse in scope has a span with a resolved span_strong_match; every span resolves to a verse and a term.

spec.ordinal: between 1 and 3 — the base layer's first act
spec.⚠ does_not_exist_as_a_module: Today this work happens inside audit_word ('inserts + span-links in one pass'), reachable via `--skip-span-backpop`. It has no module, no process, no rules and no gate of its own — while ve_lexical, char_candidate and every pair endpoint are addressed BY IT.
spec.⚠ governs_is_a_placeholder: `raw` is wrong — spans are DERIVED, therefore base. Set only because the envelope requires a value. Blocked on open.pipeline.base-layer-carve.
what_it_owns: the span index — one addressable row per term-in-verse
span_strong_match — the field that proves the term is actually AT the verse (evidence vs reference)
span identity — the join key for ve_lexical, char_candidate, and every pair's from_span/to_span
spec.why_it_must_be_its_own_module: Because everything above joins on its output. A step that universal must be independently runnable, independently gated, and impossible to skip by a flag on someone else's module.

dependencies.subject: dep-spans-raw
dependencies.intent: Spans are derived from raw morphology, so raw must be present and complete first.
dependencies.satisfaction: module.0.spans does not run until module.1.ingest's raw layer is complete for the scope.

dependencies.subject: dep-passage-seed
dependencies.authority: passage rule v2 (candidate-driven); cycle authoritative v1 §4A
dependencies.intent: A passage is a run of consecutive CANDIDATE-BEARING verses, so the seed must exist before passages can be built.
dependencies.satisfaction: module.3.passage does not run until module.2.seed is complete for the scope.

dependencies.subject: dep-lexical-spans
dependencies.authority: plan §3.4.2 ('the span-id is the join key'); ent.lexical.record identity
dependencies.intent: ★ THE DEPENDENCY THE PIPELINE DID NOT STATE. The lexical read is ABOUT a span; without spans there is nothing to read.
dependencies.satisfaction: module.5.lexical does not run until spans exist for the scope.

spec.why_halt_not_auto: If spans are missing, something upstream went wrong — silently building them mid-read would mask the fault. Halt and say so.
spec.⚠ today_this_edge_is_invisible: The plan's flow (§3.2) runs 1 -> 2 -> {3,4} -> 5, with no span step. The dependency is real and satisfied by accident, because span-linking is bundled into module 1. An accidental dependency is one nothing protects.

dependencies.subject: dep-lexical-passage
dependencies.authority: plan §3.2; wa-verse-analysis-method-v1 (the read unit is the passage)
dependencies.intent: The read unit is the passage, so passages must exist before lexical runs.
dependencies.satisfaction: module.5.lexical does not run until module.3.passage is complete for the scope.

dependencies.subject: dep-lexical-stem
dependencies.intent: The stem master supports the lexical read's morphological dimensions.
dependencies.satisfaction: module.5.lexical does not run until module.4.stem is complete for the scope.

dependencies.subject: dep-char-lexical
dependencies.intent: Characteristics are derived from validated lexical reads.
dependencies.satisfaction: module.6.characteristic does not run until module.5.lexical is complete for the scope.

dependencies.subject: dep-findings-validation
dependencies.intent: Findings are drawn only from VALIDATED lexicals — the enforcement point of 'done = validity, not coverage'.
dependencies.satisfaction: module.9.findings does not run until module.7.validation passes for the scope.

spec.why_halt: Producing findings from unvalidated reads is the exact failure the 2026-07-14 audit exposed — 8 dimensions failing their own rules while the layer read as complete. Never auto-activate past this.

module_gates.subject: mgate-ingest-oracle
module_gates.intent: No ingest is marked done until its rows reconcile against STEP's reported total.
module_gates.satisfaction: gate.step.cap-exhausted passes for every query in the run.

module_gates.subject: mgate-ingest-available
module_gates.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-15 ('Check site is up is a pre-requisite for running raw processes - on error stop and warn researcher')
module_gates.intent: The STEP pre-flight is a PRE-REQUISITE for any raw process, not a runtime check.

spec.note: on_fail = halt AND warn the researcher — a raw process without its source is not a slow run, it is a wrong one.

module_gates.subject: mgate-lexical-ledger
module_gates.intent: A lexical read is not done until its ledger is complete — the definition of done for the layer that failed.
module_gates.satisfaction: gate.lexical.ledger-complete passes for every span in scope.

module_gates.subject: mgate-seed-integrity
module_gates.intent: The integrity invariant the researcher named: a candidate with no verse-record is a violation, not a gap.

spec.note: halt and restore — repair before proceeding.
